Jess should weigh four things: cash flow (whether rent covers mortgage, condo fees, property tax and insurance with a buffer for vacancies), taxes (renting can cost her the principal-residence exemption for those years and rental income is taxable), her market view (selling locks in today's price, holding is a bet on appreciation), and landlord effort plus whether she might move back.
Action: None; a one-hour session with a fee-only planner or accountant is worth suggesting before she decides.

Arctic AC is a classic; the coat at the desk says it all. If it keeps up, a facilities request usually gets it nudged a few degrees. The pricing-page check on the plan table is still running and I'll tell you only if something changed.
Action: None unless you want me to file a facilities ticket.

I don't have this year's opening date saved, so I'll check the market's own listing rather than guess. When I have it I'll tell you the date and hours.
Action: Look up the Leslieville farmers market opening day and hours for this year, report back, and add it to the calendar if you want it there.

Booking 25 minutes with Olivia and Aisha on the 9th at 3:30pm, 15:30-15:55, with your agenda: 1) where certification stands, 2) what sales can and can't say, 3) next checkpoint. I won't put a GA date in the invite, so nothing goes to sales ahead of that conversation.
Action: Check Olivia's and Aisha's calendars for 15:30 on the next 9th, send the invite with the agenda, and tell you if anyone has a conflict.
